title: MessagesStore/receipt CBOR decode is laxer than Python oracle
description:
File: rust/lichen-client/src/msg.rs (post_inbox, ReceiptStore::post, Inbox/Sent/DeliveryReceipt::from_cbor)

Python mutation decode (_decode_single_cbor in python/src/lichen/coap/resources/cbor_validation.py) rejects:

- trailing bytes after the first CBOR item
- duplicate map keys
- CBOR tags
- payloads over 4096 bytes, depth > 16, maps > 64 entries, arrays > 256

Rust uses ciborium::from_reader on the slice with no leftover check. Duplicate keys become a Vec of pairs; map_get/set_key use the first match; a later duplicate remains on the wire. Trailing bytes are ignored. Tags may decode as Value::Tag.

Parser differential vs the Python MessagesResource / MessageReceiptsResource that consume test/vectors/messaging.json. Duplicate keys are a classic first-vs-last security split. Sibling lichen-client decoders (config.rs, radio_config.rs) already reject trailing bytes via Cursor position.

Fix: decode one item, require reader.position() == len, reject duplicate keys and tags, and apply the same size/depth caps as the Python oracle.

Perspectives: security, robustness, correctness.
